statement_en: Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$ where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).
statement_lean:
open scoped Classical

theorem erdos_62104 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ f : ℕ → Fin k,
      c * N ≤ (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun n =>
        ∃ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∃ b ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
          a ≠ b ∧ f a = f b ∧ a + b = n).card : ℝ) := by
  sorry
